description: A denial that says the care was not medically necessary: the appeal path and deadline for the plan type, the rule that the appeal considers new evidence (such as a letter from the person's doctor), the right to the claim file, and a draft appeal built for this reason. It does not judge whether the care was necessary. Example questions: insurance says it's not medically necessary; how to fight a medical necessity denial; what to put in an appeal for a necessity denial.

letter_date.description: Date printed on the letter, if the reader missed it

received_date.description: Day the person actually received the letter, if they say

stage.description: pre_service = prior authorization, post_service = a claim for care already given, concurrent = ongoing care being cut

urgent.description: True only if the person or their doctor says waiting could seriously harm their health. Never infer it.

name: medical_necessity_denial
title: Denied as not medically necessary
